name: Alex Rivera
summary: Backend engineer who builds payment and logistics systems in Python and Go.

projects.name: shop-api
projects.description: Order and payment API for a small retail business.
bullets: Built the order and checkout API in FastAPI with 24 endpoints, backed by PostgreSQL and Stripe webhooks
Wrote pytest coverage for refunds and failed payments, and ran the suite on every push with GitHub Actions
Added structured request logging and a health check endpoint used by the deploy pipeline
evidence: 24 endpoints: counted route decorators in app/routes

projects.name: logsift
projects.description: Command-line tool that filters and summarises application logs.
bullets: Implemented streaming filters that process 1 GB log files without loading them into memory
Added saved queries and a TUI table view, with 38 tests covering parsing and filter combinations
Packaged the tool as a single static binary and published Linux and macOS builds with GoReleaser
evidence: 38 tests: counted Test functions in the repository

projects.name: invoice-tracker
projects.description: Self-hosted invoicing app for freelancers, with recurring invoices and PDF export.
bullets: Built recurring invoice generation with idempotent runs, so a retry never sends a client a duplicate invoice
Added a PDF export that renders in under a second using WeasyPrint templates
Built a customer portal with HTMX that updates invoice status without a full page reload
evidence: Idempotent runs: tasks/generate.py and its tests

projects.name: webhook-relay
projects.description: Service that receives carrier webhooks, verifies signatures and forwards events to internal queues.
bullets: Built signature verification and retry handling for 6 carrier webhook formats
Queued failed deliveries in Redis with exponential backoff and a replay command for operators
Wrote integration tests that run the service against a local Redis and a mock carrier
